overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of critical phenomenology's extensions of the body-subject. You'll be asked about Fanon's historico-racial schema, Young's inhibited intentionality and ambiguous transcendence, Ahmed's orientation, and the aims of critical phenomenology.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: How does Fanon's historico-racial schema differ from the body schema?

options.html: It's a conscious belief, while the body schema is unconscious
options.text: It's a conscious belief, while the body schema is unconscious
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both are lived bodily. The difference is where their elements come from.

options.html: It's inherited genetically, while the body schema is learned
options.text: It's inherited genetically, while the body schema is learned
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Fanon describes a social and historical schema, not a genetic one.

options.html: Its elements come from others' stories, images, and looks
options.text: Its elements come from others' stories, images, and looks
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The body schema forms from one's own movements. The historico-racial schema is woven by a racializing society.

options.html: It governs only speech, while the body schema governs movement
options.text: It governs only speech, while the body schema governs movement
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It shapes how a racialized person lives their body as a whole.

forms.stemHtml: A woman sees a heavy box as something she can lift, yet at the same moment feels she can't, and lifts it with her arms alone. Which of Young's concepts describes this?

options.html: Discontinuous unity alone, since only her arms move
options.text: Discontinuous unity alone, since only her arms move
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The arms-only lift shows discontinuous unity, but the split "I can" and "I cannot" is inhibited intentionality.

options.html: Inhibited intentionality: "I can" undercut by "I cannot"
options.text: Inhibited intentionality: "I can" undercut by "I cannot"
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Her directedness toward the task is real but held back from full commitment.

options.html: An epidermal racial schema displacing her body schema
options.text: An epidermal racial schema displacing her body schema
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's Fanon's concept. Young calls this inhibited intentionality.

options.html: A lack of motor intentionality toward the box
options.text: A lack of motor intentionality toward the box
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. She is directed at the box. Her directedness is inhibited, not absent.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe critical phenomenology? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It attends to contingent social structures that shape experience
options.text: It attends to contingent social structures that shape experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Guenther calls these quasi-transcendental structures.

options.html: It uses phenomenological description of lived experience
options.text: It uses phenomenological description of lived experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It describes experience from within, as phenomenology does.

options.html: It aims at changing the structures it describes
options.text: It aims at changing the structures it describes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Guenther describes it as a practice aimed at restructuring the world.

options.html: It treats social structures as conditions of all possible experience
options.text: It treats social structures as conditions of all possible experience
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The structures are "quasi"-transcendental: contingent and historical, though deeply shaping.

options.html: It is agreed to be a complete break with classical phenomenology
options.text: It is agreed to be a complete break with classical phenomenology
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Whether it completes or breaks with the classical project is debated.

forms.stemHtml: What is Young's term for the way feminine bodily existence reaches toward the world while also living the body as a thing? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It's the first of Young's three modalities of feminine motility.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Young calls this ambiguous transcendence.

options.html: A person's sexual identity, and nothing more
options.text: A person's sexual identity, and nothing more
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Sexual orientation is one case of orientation, which is a general account of bodily directedness.

options.html: The body's position in objective, measurable space
options.text: The body's position in objective, measurable space
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Orientation concerns direction toward objects, not coordinates.

options.html: A private attitude with no effect on what bodies can do
options.text: A private attitude with no effect on what bodies can do
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Orientation shapes what is within reach, so it affects what bodies can do.

options.html: How bodies are directed toward some objects and not others
options.text: How bodies are directed toward some objects and not others
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Orientation, sustained by lines, shapes what is within a body's reach.

title: Critical Phenomenology
